nodes.description: Public mapping address => uint256 holding token balances of each account.
Public string token name 'PORTUGAL_WINS'.
Public string token symbol 'PORWII'.
Public uint8 number of decimals (18).
Public uint256 total token supply, minted to the deployer/caller.
Public nested mapping owner => spender => uint256 approved spending amounts.
Public function (misnamed as constructor) that assigns the whole totalSupply to msg.sender and emits Transfer; callable by anyone at any time.
Public transfer of value tokens from msg.sender to 'to', with balance checks and balance updates.
Public approval of 'spender' to spend 'value' tokens on behalf of msg.sender.
Public transfer of 'value' tokens from 'from' to 'to' using allowance[from][msg.sender].
Caller-controlled address used for balances, allowances and initialization.
balanceOf[msg.sender] -= value and balanceOf[to] += value inside transfer, unchecked arithmetic.
balanceOf[from] -= value, balanceOf[to] += value and allowance[from][msg.sender] -= value inside transferFrom, unchecked arithmetic.
Anyone can call SimpleERC20Token() to re-mint/overwrite balanceOf[msg.sender] with totalSupply: missing access control on initialization.
Recipient address parameter of transfer.
Amount parameter of transfer.
Spender address parameter of approve.
Allowance amount parameter of approve.
Source address parameter of transferFrom.
Destination address parameter of transferFrom.
Amount parameter of transferFrom.
Return flag of transfer, always set to true.
Return flag of approve, always set to true.
Return flag of transferFrom, always set to true.

edges.reason: msg.sender is used to assign the whole totalSupply to the caller inside SimpleERC20Token.
msg.sender identifies the debited balance and the event emitter in transfer.
msg.sender is the owner key written into allowance in approve.
msg.sender is used as the spender key for allowance checks in transferFrom.
totalSupply value is read during initialization to seed balanceOf[msg.sender].
Initialization writes totalSupply into balanceOf[msg.sender].
Initialization routine is publicly callable with no guard, letting any caller mint/overwrite balances.
transfer feeds 'value' into unchecked balance increments/decrements.
transfer reads and writes balanceOf for sender and recipient.
approve writes the allowance mapping for msg.sender and spender.
transferFrom feeds 'value' into unchecked balance and allowance decrements.
transferFrom reads and writes balanceOf[from] and balanceOf[to].
transferFrom reads and decrements allowance[from][msg.sender].
balanceOf subtraction/addition in transfer can underflow or overflow balances.
balanceOf subtraction/addition in transferFrom can underflow or overflow balances.
allowance[from][msg.sender] -= value in transferFrom can underflow.
transfer recipient parameter is written into balanceOf[to].
transfer amount parameter is the value checked and moved.
approve spender parameter indexes the allowance mapping.
approve amount parameter is stored in allowance[msg.sender][spender].
transferFrom source address is debited and used for the allowance lookup.
transferFrom destination address is credited in balanceOf[to].
transferFrom amount parameter drives the balance and allowance arithmetic.
transfer return flag depends on successful completion of its balance updates.
approve return flag reports success of the allowance write.
transferFrom return flag reports success of the transfer and allowance updates.

normalization_plan.reason: Recipient address operand only meaningful as an argument of transfer; fold into the transfer function node.
Amount operand feeds directly into the unchecked balance arithmetic of transfer.
Spender index operand is only used inside approve's allowance write.
Allowance amount operand is only used inside approve's state write.
Source address operand is only used inside transferFrom's balance and allowance logic.
Destination address operand is only used inside transferFrom's credit operation.
Amount operand feeds directly into the unchecked balance/allowance arithmetic of transferFrom.
Return flag is a direct output of the transfer function; fold into the function node.
Return flag is a direct output of the approve function; fold into the function node.
Return flag is a direct output of the transferFrom function; fold into the function node.
